subject: Private deploy pricing — exit guardrail & operator license mix
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@neohosp.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-26T16:12:00-04:00
Subject: Private deployment commercial — follow-ups

Hi David,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up on a few pricing/packaging items we need clarified before we prepare an LOI:

- Platform fee amortization: do you offer a staggered amortization if we commit 24 vs 36 months? We want the math to show on our P&L.
- Operator vs site license mix: our infra team expects ~8 A100-equivalent GPUs to start. Is it possible to buy operator licenses for a subset of nodes and keep the rest under the platform fee?
- Exit guardrails: what options do you provide if we need to scale down after 12 months (credits, prorated refunds, migration assistance)?
- Support tiers: can we see a simple mapping of SLA / oncall entitlements by tier? procurement would like a one-page table.

I've attached our internal procurement checklist (snippet) and can share the SOW template if helpful. For now, attaching the initial term sheet request as a stub.

Can you loop in whoever owns commercial constructs?

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
VP, Operations
Neohosp

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (AE) and Marissa (Sales Ops) to propose concrete options. Quick clarifying questions so we align the examples to your finance team:

1) Commitment horizon: do you want examples for 12/24/36 months or focus on 24 vs 36 only?
2) Starting capacity: you mentioned ~8 A100-equivalent GPUs — is that steady-state or pilot (i.e., will you ramp)?
3) Air-gapped / air-gapped components: is there any strict airgap requirement for the initial pilot? That affects operator-license vs platform-fee split.

We'll produce a short appendix with: amortization examples, three packaging mixes (operator-heavy / hybrid / platform-first), and an exit-guardrail matrix (credits, migration assistance window, data export SLA).

I'll also attach a draft term sheet (internal, illustrative) for discussion.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Private deployment commercial — follow-ups

Elena — thanks, I sketched three practical packaging options below (numbers illustrative). I recommend we present 24- and 36-month amortization lines.

Option A — Platform-first (lower upfront, higher platform fee)
- Operator licenses: 0
- Platform fee (monthly, amortized): $42,500 / month (24m) or $31,900 / month (36m)
- Support tier: Standard SRE (8x5) included; Oncall add-on available
- Exit: 6-month notice, 50% credit on remaining platform fees for year 2 if canceled after month 12

Option B — Hybrid (recommended for Neohosp pilot -> scale)
- Operator licenses: 4 operator seats (cover 50% of GPUs) licensed as site operators (one-time license amortized over term)
- Remaining capacity on platform-fee basis
- Platform fee: $27,000 / month (24m) or $20,000 / month (36m) + operator license amortization ($9,000 spread over 24m)
- Support tier: Premium SRE (8x5 + priority incident triage); includes 2x guaranteed oncall rotations per quarter
- Exit: migration assistance included (up to 80 engineering hours) + one-time migration credit equal to 25% of remaining operator license value

Option C — Operator-first (higher upfront, lower ongoing)
- Operator licenses: 8 operator seats (covers all GPUs) one-time license amortized
- Platform fee: nominal ($6,500 / month) for control plane only
- Support tier: Enterprise SRE (24x7) recommended for full-operator installs
- Exit: operator license transferrable to fallback partner but no refund; migration assistance available as paid SOW

Support tiers (summary table — I attached a short spreadsheet):
- Standard: 8x5, email SLAs, 24-hour critical response window
- Premium: 8x5 + priority triage, 4-hour critical response
- Enterprise: 24x7 oncall, dedicated SRE engagement, 1-hour critical response

Notes on amortization: we can show line-item amortization in your P&L by splitting operator license capex (one-time) vs platform fee opex. For procurement-friendly reporting, the hybrid approach usually balances cash flow and operational risk during pilot-to-scale.

I'll attach support_tiers_table.xlsx and a sample amortization workbook. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the math.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive — Redwoo d Inference
